newsitem.title: UK: Telewest residential clients up 34 pct in YR.
newsitem.headline: Telewest residential clients up 34 pct in YR.

text.p: Telewest Communications said on Wednesday its total residential customer base rose 33.8 percent to 768,755 in 1996 after a "very strong" fourth quarter.

Telewest, whose position as Britain's biggest cable operator will be eclipsed in spring by new cable giant Cable and Wireless Communications, said half of its clients now took both cable TV and telephony services -- a trend it wants to build on.

"We have seen growth across all areas, reflecting the efforts we have put into improving customer service, marketing and packaging," acting chief executive officer Stephen Davidson said in a statement.

Releasing fourth quarter and full-year statistics, Telewest said Cable TV customers rose by 31.5 percent year-on-year to 528,142. In the fourth quarter, 70,000 customers were added compared with 43,000 in the same period last year.
Cable TV churn levels, when customers cancel subscriptions, fell seven percent but were still at 33.4 percent.
Chief financial officer Charles Burdick told Reuters that the company was looking to bring churn levels to the mid-to-low 20s, a target the company should reach either this year or next.
"If we're not there in 1997 we will be there in 1998," he said. "It's a very important indicator of customer satisfaction ...and a priority is to see it improving."
Telewest said it had 627,009 telephony customers -- 45.5 percent more than last year. Over 69,500 lines were added in the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with 62,500 in 1995.
The group added that its Centrex products for business customers had encouraged 27,802 new lines during the year and total lines were up 69.5 percent to 67,823 on December 1995.
Telewest has now laid cable past about 2.5 million of the just under four million homes in its franchise area, raising its "network build" to 65 percent in cable terms.
But penetration -- a key measure of the proportion of those homes that subscribe to a cable service out of all those offered it -- has barely risen.
For the company's television service, penetration now stands at 22.6 percent -- 0.7 percentage points up -- while its telephone service saw penetration rise 1.5 percentage points to 27.5 percent.
